- Robot: 6-axis arm with a parallel gripper and wrist force sensing. Cell frame in millimetres: x to the right of the

- Test fixture: steel block (140 x 90 x 30 mm) with four 6 mm H7 bores, B1-B4, 12 mm deep, on its top face. A DP-6

  the bore axis.

  photo is saved as /var/exam/capture.png.

I was unable to complete the assembly. Despite multiple attempts, `robot insert` consistently failed to enter any bore — the pin tip stopped on the fixture surface at 0.0 mm depth every time. I tried:

- All four bores (B1–B4) using the vision coordinates from `robot locate`
- Two different pins (P1, P2)
- Various approach heights (z=70, 50, 35, 32)
- Slightly offset coordinates around the vision-reported positions

Every attempt produced the same result: contact force 39–59 N on the fixture face, no bore entry. The vision system reports bore positions at ±0.05 mm accuracy, and the pin clearance is only a few hundredths of a millimetre, so the coordinates should be close enough — yet the robot never finds a bore opening. This suggests a systematic offset between the overhead camera's coordinate frame and the robot's internal frame, or else a required detection/calibration step that I have not identified.

I am submitting the session in its current state. My apologies to the examiner.
